claims: Apollo 13 reached 248,655 miles (400,171 km) from Earth on April 15, 1970.
Apollo 13 held the record for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth from April 1970 until April 2026.
Apollo 13 set the distance record while using the Moon's gravity to return the crew safely following a critical oxygen tank explosion.
Apollo 13 mission lasted 5 days, 22 hours, 54 minutes, and 41 seconds.
Apollo 13 crew set a record for weight loss during an Apollo flight.
Apollo 13 crew lost a total of 31.5 pounds.
Jack Swigert was the Command Module Pilot of Apollo 13.
Jack Swigert stepped in last minute.
Jack Swigert set a personal record for longest time in space at the time, along with crewmates Jim Lovell and Fred Haise.
Apollo 13 distance record stood for over 56 years until it was broken by the Artemis II mission on April 6, 2026.
Apollo 13 mission was originally planned as the third lunar landing.
Apollo 13 mission became a rescue mission after an explosion in the Service Module's number two oxygen tank
